turn_text: Today's Acropulse update is brought to you by Curious Plot, a full-service marketing, communications, and consulting agency driven to find what's next for food and agriculture clients. Learn more online at curiousplot.agency. Good Friday afternoon, I'm Hannah Paggle. The next deadline for a government shutdown is on November 17, which is just two weeks away. Congress has been working to pass more appropriations bills on both sides of the chamber, but an Iowa Republican says more time is going to be needed. Ashley Henson sits on the House Ag Appropriations Subcommittee. Speaking on this week's Agarpulse Newsmakers, Henson says a continuing resolution is going to be needed to allow the House and the Senate to finish its work.

I think by the end of this week, we should have eight of the appropriations bills out of the house, which I think is a really good amount of progress. We're going to be back here next week, again, continuing that work. So we will need the time to conference these bills. And I think that our new speaker, Mike Johnson, I'm very thankful that we have someone now leading our chamber again. But he has really expressed that we need to make sure we continue to have leverage to negotiate with the Senate and the Biden White House. And I think that the CR and continuing to do our work and pass our bills is going to be my top priority in the next couple of weeks.

Hinson says, besides funding the government, passing a farm bill is on her top priority list. In conversations with colleagues, she says there is still support to get a farm bill on the house floor by the end of December. But that an extension would also be welcomed.

I think that there would be appetite judging by what we've seen out of the last couple of extensions. I think there is appetite to do a shorter term extension. Maybe it is a year. I'm not sure what the timeframe will be, but we absolutely need to make sure that those programs are in place. Obviously, again, that September 30th deadline came and went. And while those programs are not expired yet, we understand the urgency in that December 31st deadline is approaching quickly.

TA Hawks with Monument Advocacy and Anne Stuckel at the National Farmers' Union were also on this week's show to further discuss the ag appropriations bill process and biofuels policy. Tune in Saturday morning to watch this week's show at 11 a.m. Eastern, 8 a.m. Pacific on RFD-TV. USDA says the Women, Infants and Children's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, commonly referred to as WIC, is only reaching half of eligible participants. USDA released a new report that highlights participation levels of the WIC program. Stacy Dean is USDA's Deputy Undersecretary for Food, Nutrition, and Consumer Services. In an interview with Agarpulse, she says USDA needs to keep working to promote this program.

But the report that we put out really speaks to a challenge that WIC has, which is we're not reaching all eligible. In fact, we really, on average, basically only reach about half of eligible people, which means that we have a lot of work to do to connect this incredible evidence-based program to families in need. there are nearly 12 million eligible pregnant women, nursing mothers, and young children who can participate in the program. But only 51% of them are actively using the program. Dean says Congress needs to continue to support the program.
